english: $$F(x)=\begin{vmatrix}\sqrt{1+x} & \sin x & \log_{e}(1+x)\\ \tan x & e^{\sin x} & x^{2}\\ 1-\cos x & e^{x}-1 & \dfrac{1}{1+x}\end{vmatrix}$$
hindi: माना कि $F:(-1,1)\to\mathbb{R}$ निम्न द्वारा परिभाषित है
$$F(x)=\begin{vmatrix}\sqrt{1+x} & \sin x & \log_{e}(1+x)\\ \tan x & e^{\sin x} & x^{2}\\ 1-\cos x & e^{x}-1 & \dfrac{1}{1+x}\end{vmatrix}$$
solution: Differentiate row by row: $F'(x)=\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}+\Delta_{3}$, where $\Delta_{i}$ has row $i$ differentiated
solution_full: For a determinant whose entries are differentiable functions, $F'(x)=\Delta_{1}(x)+\Delta_{2}(x)+\Delta_{3}(x)$, where $\Delta_{i}$ is $F$ with the $i$-th row replaced by its derivative and the other rows unchanged. All entries are differentiable on $(-1,1)$.

Derivatives of the rows: $R_{1}'=\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1+x}},\cos x,\dfrac{1}{1+x}\right)$, $R_{2}'=\left(\sec^{2}x,\cos x\,e^{\sin x},2x\right)$, $R_{3}'=\left(\sin x,e^{x},-\dfrac{1}{(1+x)^{2}}\right)$. At $x=0$: $R_{1}'(0)=\left(\dfrac12,1,1\right)$, $R_{2}'(0)=(1,1,0)$, $R_{3}'(0)=(0,1,-1)$.
Hence $F'(0)=\dfrac12+1-1=\dfrac12=0.50$. (Because the other two rows are rows of the identity, each $\Delta_{i}(0)$ is just the $i$-th diagonal entry of $R_{i}'(0)$.)
originality_note: New: a determinant of unrelated transcendental entries that equals the identity matrix at x = 0, so the row-by-row derivative at 0 collapses to the derivatives of the diagonal entries (way 4, hidden structure). Closest known: textbook 'differentiate the determinant' exercises and the JEE problem with rows (cos x, x, 1), (2 sin x, x^2, 2x), (tan x, x, 1). Different because: expanding F is long, while the identity at 0 makes each of the three row-derivative determinants triangular.

concept_use.Differentiation of Determinants: F'(0) is computed as the sum of the three determinants obtained by differentiating one row at a time.
